analysis.title: 3 EMEA EQD Bullets
key_insights: Equity volatility was broadly stable, but November downside wings remained rich after a large put trade on 10/27. 10-delta downside is expensive versus Dec/Jan, which may give systematic and risk-premium sellers a chance to sell one-month downside as the post-trade repricing fades.
Positioning is viewed as relatively well hedged against Iran-US risk. Spot is already lower and vol/skew is elevated, which reduces the likelihood of a disorderly volatility shock.
Profit-taking on existing put protection is flagged as a possible flow if tensions develop without an immediate escalation.
European Banks: Gerry Fowler expects a rebound after a ~12.5% drop since mid-August, citing lower yields and a smaller French bond risk premium.
Heidelberg Materials (HEI GY): downgrade fears look overdone, and an in-line Q3 on 4 Nov 2026 could de-risk FY26 guidance and squeeze bearish positioning.
Autos led European thematics (UBXEAUTO +2.01%), supported by a euro down more than 5% against the dollar YTD, which lifts the earnings outlook for exporters during peak Q3 reporting season.

MBG GY Q3 showed a 4.5% revenue decline and a deepening China slump, but this appears largely priced in after the 10/27 guidance cut. The market is focused on the announced cost overhaul and productivity measures.

AI Winners outperformed (UBXEAIW +1.83%) after ASM International raised its 2027 sales outlook to above €5.7 billion from €4.6 billion on AI-driven demand for chip tools. ASML traded higher in sympathy.

Chemicals fell (UBXECHEM -1.32%). BASF dropped as much as 1.8% despite a Q3 earnings beat on softer Q4 guidance and weakness in Agriculture Solutions. Corbion fell as much as 6.5% on weaker nine-month organic sales growth and the collapse of its PLA business sale.

Software lagged (UBXESOFT -1.96%) on cautious positioning ahead of Alphabet and Microsoft earnings after the close, with investors wary that AI capex commentary could reprice growth expectations for European software.
